clue.text: Leaning over, swerves when cornering intense — here?

definitions.text: Leaning over, swerves when cornering intense — here?

indicators.note: something leaning right over ends up turned the other way, so the word for intense is read backwards
to corner something is to trap it, so the word for swerves closes around the other piece

blocks.note: to sway is to swerve from side to side
deep feelings are intense ones

explanation.surface: A motorcycle racer tilts over and slides round a tight bend at full throttle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a picture of the place: riders on this track lean over and slide through every bend at high speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedway is motorcycle racing on an oval dirt track, where riders famously lean and skid through every corner.

clue.text: Go, old man

blocks.note: first meaning: to go briefly somewhere, as in nipping out to the shops
second meaning: an informal word for father

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words sound like an instruction to an elderly man; they are two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: You can pop round to a friend's, and Pop is a familiar name for one's father, whom slang also calls the old man.

clue.text: Lowest characters in the Bronx, public square, will stand out

indicators.note: in a down entry the lowest letters of each word are its final ones, so only the last letter of each is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A New York public square will be the place that makes an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowest' fits a down clue, where the end of each word is its bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding, doing better than everyone else around you.

clue.text: Puzzle had screw loose, or had cracked

indicators.note: a screw that has come loose rattles about out of place, so these letters get rearranged
something cracked is broken apart, so this short word joins the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a puzzle had either a screw loose or had cracked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'loose' and 'cracked' signal rearrangement, one for each part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordsearch is a puzzle in which listed words must be found hidden in a grid of letters.

clue.text: Every so often, noble lines wise to say?

indicators.note: to say means as spoken, so the word wise is taken for how it sounds
lining something means sitting along both its sides, so one piece gets letters at either edge

blocks.note: wise sounds like Ys, two of the letter Y
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A wise aristocrat's verses are recited every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Wise said aloud is 'Y's', a pair of Ys, which sit on either side of EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens once a year recurs at intervals, so it occurs every so often, though the clue stretches the sense.

clue.text: See 18
Said captain associated with Scott's porridge

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the captain's name is taken only for its sound

blocks.note: Captain Lawrence Oates died on Scott's 1912 Antarctic expedition

explanation.surface: Scott's porridge, a brand name, linked to one of his officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Oates walked out into the blizzard on Robert Falcon Scott's doomed polar journey; Scott's Porage Oats is also a real breakfast brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is made from rolled oats, so the grain stands in for the dish by close association.

clue.text: Daughter dressed by fashion designer and partner formerly referencing method

indicators.note: someone dressed by others is clothed by them, so the other letters wrap around this one

blocks.note: Pierre Cardin, the French couturier
a former partner is an ex
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl is dressed by a couturier and a former lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Cardin was a French fashion designer; both he and the ex 'dress' the daughter by sitting either side of her.
explanation.definitionFit: A card index is a system of filing cards used to look up and cross-refer information.

clue.text: Dependent Arab, a thieving felon at heart — with this?

definitions.text: Dependent Arab, a thieving felon at heart — with this?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter of felon is kept
something thieving takes things inside, so the other letters pocket the felon's centre

blocks.note: a dependent person is kept by another
an Omani is an Arab from Oman
taken as written
the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A felon who steals, though kept and Arab, is driven by some compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: The felon's heart is stolen into the string just after its first letter; the whole clue then asks what condition would make one thieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleptomania is a compulsive urge to steal, the condition a thieving felon might have.

clue.text: Opener turning on lids

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
caps are lids on bottles and jars

explanation.surface: Someone unscrewing lids, perhaps a jar opener twisting them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' looks like a jar opener; it is the definition, a thing that opens up space.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer is a piece inserted to keep two parts apart, so it opens a gap between them.

clue.text: See 25
Without cunning, cunningly alters as a fox?

indicators.note: doing something cunningly means craftily rearranging it, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
the fox is proverbially sly

explanation.surface: A naive person versus a fox that changes things craftily.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'cunning' is a trap: the first is the definition's opposite, the second the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Artlessly means in a guileless, innocent way, with no trickery at all.

clue.text: Place, an untidy field, for the workers

indicators.note: an untidy thing is messed up and out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a rank is a place in a hierarchy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A messy field is a place set aside for labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: Anfield is also Liverpool's football ground, a tempting extra reading for a solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and file are ordinary members of a body, the workers as opposed to the leaders.

clue.text: Number 3 together with 23 in conference?

indicators.note: a conference is a meeting for talking, so the two answers are taken as they sound when spoken

blocks.note: the answers at 3-down and 23-down, said aloud, sound like the Roman numerals for forty and twenty, which total this

explanation.surface: Two delegates, numbers 3 and 23, join forces at a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 3-down is EXCEL, said aloud 'XL' or 40; 23-down is EXECS, said 'X-X' or 20. Add them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty is simply a number, the sum of the two Roman numerals heard in the cross-referenced answers.

clue.text: Pet needing a vet ringed? I say!

blocks.note: an animal needing a vet is ill
a ring is a band, and being ringed puts the sick piece inside it
coo is an exclamation of surprise, like I say

explanation.surface: A sick pet has to see a vet who rings it; what a fuss!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is a verb here, not an animal, and 'ringed' supplies the ring itself as well as placing the sick part inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to kiss and cuddle, and to bill and coo is to murmur and caress like courting doves.

clue.text: Funny old man thinking of the conquerors?

blocks.note: first meaning: the late British slapstick comedian of film and stage
second meaning: the knowledge held by the ... who conquered England in 1066

explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a much-loved British comic actor; read literally his name is the wisdom of Normans.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian was a funny man who lived to 95, and Norman wisdom would be the thinking of the 1066 conquerors.

clue.text: Speculator who's done well to save European parliament building

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safe inside, so the other words hold the abbreviation for European

blocks.note: someone who has done well has become rich
a stag buys new share issues to sell quickly at a profit
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A successful investor rescues a European parliament building.
explanation.walkthrough: In City jargon a stag is a speculator in new share issues; the European letter goes in just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag in Berlin is the building that houses Germany's parliament, the Bundestag.

clue.text: See 15
Money for jam — something with it?

blocks.note: first meaning: a British idiom for an easy task or easily earned reward
second meaning: a slice of sponge that might come with jam in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to jam: a cake with jam in it, such as a Victoria sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both money for jam and a piece of cake are idioms for something very easy, and a cake portion often contains jam.

clue.text: As locks may be loose, bog's secured

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the word for bog encloses the word for loose

blocks.note: a fen is marshy, boggy ground
lax means slack or loose

explanation.surface: Loose hair, as a door lock or a bog may be secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door fastenings next to 'secured'; here they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaxen describes pale yellow hair, the colour of processed flax fibre, so locks may well be flaxen.

clue.text: 'I have had a most rare vision', for example — that's what it's all about

definitions.text: 'I have had a most rare vision', for example

blocks.clueFragment: 'I have had a most rare vision', for example
blocks.note: first meaning: a speech given to ... the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream
second meaning: the fundamental point of a matter

explanation.walkthrough: Bottom says the quoted words on waking after his transformation into an ass, so they are Bottom's line.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line is the essential, decisive point, literally the final figure of an account.

clue.text: State in Colorado had Iowa on the retreat

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the next run of words, spanning their boundaries
retreating means going back, so the concealed letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word, all of the second, the first of the third

explanation.surface: A battle report where Iowa's forces fall back from Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: With two states already named, a solver looks for a definition among them; the answer is a third state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the north-west, famous for potatoes.

clue.text: Local area in blue and orange all but finished after redevelopment

indicators.note: all but finished means nearly complete, so the final letter of orange is dropped
redevelopment rebuilds things in a new layout, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A district repainted blue and orange is nearly done after regeneration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is the British word for one's neighbourhood pub, not a neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a British pub, so it is an area of the local.

clue.text: Suits: a hundred in the other wardrobe at the back, turned up

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the numeral goes inside the word for the other
the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter of wardrobe is used
in a down entry turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: 'the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hundred garments hung up at the back of a wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like clothes in the wardrobe; it means business people. C goes inside SEX after its S, E follows, and the lot reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Suits is slang for executives or managers, named after their business attire.

clue.text: See 20
US lawman using remarkable tact with traitor when missing article stolen by Mickey Mouse chap?

indicators.note: remarkable here means notably altered, so the letters are rearranged into a new order
missing means lacking, so the letter for the article is taken away
something stolen is carried off inside the thief, so the outer name surrounds the rest

blocks.note: Walt Disney created Mickey Mouse
taken as written
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A US prosecutor tactfully handles a traitor caught pilfering from a cartoon creator.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two As in the fodder goes, and the shuffled letters split the cartoon-maker's surname after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A district attorney is the public prosecutor for a county or district in the United States.

clue.text: Shabby kidnapping of that man by Mafia boss

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds the victim captive inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a capo is a Mafia chief
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A shoddy abduction of a man carried out by a Mafia boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for cheap and inferior, so shabby, low-quality goods are cheapo.

clue.text: Weed with OOOOOOOO counted as vegetables?

blocks.clueFragment: Weed with OOOOOOOO counted as vegetables?
blocks.note: surface reading: a gardener weeding among a crop of vegetables
setter's reading: add a count of the letters, eight Os, and the spoken result names a root vegetable

explanation.surface: Some weed, a string of Os, somehow counted as vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: POT is slang for cannabis; add 'eight Os' and you say 'pot-eight-Os', or potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, which is popularly known as weed.

clue.text: Horse with gelding on the outside?

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two ends, so only the first and last letters of gelding are kept

blocks.note: the two end letters, each written out as the name of the letter

explanation.surface: A horse, with a gelding standing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of gelding are G and G; spelling each out gives the nursery word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gee is a childish or racing-slang word for a horse, from the command gee to urge it on.

clue.text: Heavenly phenomena, beam finally having disappeared in moments so extraordinary

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word beam, so its last letter is the one meant
disappearing from something means being taken out of it, so that letter is removed
extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A light beam vanishing during extraordinary moments in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip one M from MOMENTS SO and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonset is the moon sinking below the horizon, an astronomical event seen in the sky.
